Question 1
?

Given that 2x2−9x+13(x−3)2(x+1)=A(x−3)+B(x−3)2+C(x+1),

where A, B, and C are real constants, determine the value of A⋅B⋅C.

a
 59
b
34
c
 78
d
4
e
83
Submit

decision.explanation: Multiplying by (x-3)^2(x+1) gives 2x^2-9x+13=A(x-3)(x+1)+B(x+1)+C(x-3)^2. Setting x=3 gives B=1; setting x=-1 gives C=3/2. Comparing x^2 coefficients gives A+C=2, so A=1/2. Thus ABC=(1/2)(1)(3/2)=3/4.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{2{x}^{2}-9x+13}{(x-3)^{2}(x+1)}=\frac{A}{(x-3)}+\frac{B}{(x-3)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x+1)},
$$

where $A$, $B$, and $C$ are real constants, determine the value of $A\cdot B\cdot C.$
after.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-3)^{2}(x+1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}-9x+13 & =A(x-3)(x+1)+B(x+1)+C(x-3)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=-1$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-1)^{2}-9(-1)+13 & =A(-1-3)(-1+1)+B(-1+1)+C(-1-3)^{2} \\ 2+9+13 & =16C \\ 24 & =16C \\ C & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=3$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2(3)^{2}-9(3)+13 & =A(3-3)(3+1)+B(3+1)+C(3-3)^{2} \\ 18-27+13 & =4B \\ 4 & =4B \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, letting $x=0$ and using our values for $B$ and $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2(0)^{2}-9(0)+13 & =A(0-3)(0+1)+1(0+1)+\frac{3}{2}(0-3)^{2} \\ 13 & =-3A+1+\frac{27}{2} \\ 3A & =\frac{3}{2} \\ A & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\cdot B\cdot C & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot \frac{3}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

Given that 2x2−9x+13(x−3)2(x+1)=A(x−3)+B(x−3)2+C(x+1),

where A, B, and C are real constants, determine the value of A⋅B⋅C.

a
 59
b
34
c
 78
d
4
e
83
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Multiplying both sides of the given equality by (x−3)2(x+1) gives

2x2−9x+13=A(x−3)(x+1)+B(x+1)+C(x−3)2.

Letting x=−1 gives

2(−1)2−9(−1)+13=A(−1−3)(−1+1)+B(−1+1)+C(−1−3)22+9+13=16C24=16CC=32.

Letting x=3 gives 2(3)2−9(3)+13=A(3−3)(3+1)+B(3+1)+C(3−3)218−27+13=4B4=4BB=1.

Finally, letting x=0 and using our values for B and C gives

2(0)2−9(0)+13=A(0−3)(0+1)+1(0+1)+32(0−3)213=−3A+1+2723A=32A=12.

Hence, A⋅B⋅C=12⋅1⋅32=34.

$$

where $A$, $B$, and $C$ are real constants, determine the value of $A\cdot B\cdot C.$
content.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-3)^{2}(x+1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}-9x+13 & =A(x-3)(x+1)+B(x+1)+C(x-3)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-1)^{2}-9(-1)+13 & =A(-1-3)(-1+1)+B(-1+1)+C(-1-3)^{2} \\ 2+9+13 & =16C \\ 24 & =16C \\ C & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=3$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2(3)^{2}-9(3)+13 & =A(3-3)(3+1)+B(3+1)+C(3-3)^{2} \\ 18-27+13 & =4B \\ 4 & =4B \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, letting $x=0$ and using our values for $B$ and $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2(0)^{2}-9(0)+13 & =A(0-3)(0+1)+1(0+1)+\frac{3}{2}(0-3)^{2} \\ 13 & =-3A+1+\frac{27}{2} \\ 3A & =\frac{3}{2} \\ A & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}A\cdot B\cdot C & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot \frac{3}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{4x-1}{(x-3)^{3}}=\frac{A}{x-3}+\frac{B}{(x-3)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x-3)^{3}},
$$

where $A$, $B$ and $C$ are real constants, find the value of $A\cdot B\cdot C.$
after.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-3)^{3}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-1 & =A(x-3)^{2}+B(x-3)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=3$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(3)-1 & =A(3-3)^{2}+B(3-3)+C \\ 11 & =A(0)+B(0)+C \\ C & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$ and using our value for $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)-1 & =A(0-3)^{2}+B(0-3)+11 \\ -1 & =9A-3B+11 \\ 0 & =9A-3B+12 \\ 0 & =3A-B+4 \\ B & =3A+4.\,\,(1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, letting $x=2$ and using our value for $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(2)-1 & =A(2-3)^{2}+B(2-3)+11 \\ 7 & =A-B+11 \\ 0 & =A-B+4 \\ B & =4+A.\,\,(2)\end{aligned}
$$

From $(1)$ and $(2)$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}3A+4 & =4+A \\ 2A & =0 \\ A & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the value of $A$ into $(2)$  to get the value of $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =4+0=4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\cdot B\cdot C & =0\cdot 4\cdot 11=0.\end{aligned}

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Partial Fraction Decomposition With Higher Order Factors
content.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{4x-1}{(x-3)^{3}}=\frac{A}{x-3}+\frac{B}{(x-3)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x-3)^{3}},
$$

where $A$, $B$ and $C$ are real constants, find the value of $A\cdot B\cdot C.$
content.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-3)^{3}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-1 & =A(x-3)^{2}+B(x-3)+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=3$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(3)-1 & =A(3-3)^{2}+B(3-3)+C \\ 11 & =A(0)+B(0)+C \\ C & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$ and using our value for $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)-1 & =A(0-3)^{2}+B(0-3)+11 \\ -1 & =9A-3B+11 \\ 0 & =9A-3B+12 \\ 0 & =3A-B+4 \\ B & =3A+4.\,\,(1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, letting $x=2$ and using our value for $C$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(2)-1 & =A(2-3)^{2}+B(2-3)+11 \\ 7 & =A-B+11 \\ 0 & =A-B+4 \\ B & =4+A.\,\,(2)\end{aligned}
$$

From $(1)$ and $(2)$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}3A+4 & =4+A \\ 2A & =0 \\ A & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we substitute the value of $A$ into $(2)$  to get the value of $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =4+0=4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}A\cdot B\cdot C & =0\cdot 4\cdot 11=0.\end{aligned}
$$
